title: Blockwise fusion + KV-page coordinator — kernel notes
content:
Objective:
Short notes on a blockwise-kernel fusion approach + a lightweight KV-page coordinator to reduce end-to-end p50/p95 for long-context chat workloads. Focus is on combining FlashAttention-style block matmul with a fused FFN/LayerNorm tail and a page-aware prefetch orchestration so we amortize global memory stalls across token bursts.

Context / motivation:
- We see two dominant latency sources for long-context interactive workloads: (1) attention kernel memory bandwidth + kernel launch overhead for variable token lengths, (2) KV cache page faults / PCIe/host transfers when using paged-KV for > 1B context.
- Existing FlashAttention kernels are excellent for compute-bound attention but do separate launches for attention and then post-attention ffn/ln. When paged-KV causes a few scattered page load stalls, we lose the ability to hide that latency across later ops.
- Idea: merge attention compute with the first part of FFN (or fused residual add/ln) into a blockwise fused kernel that also drives a small cooperative prefetch state machine for KV pages. This minimizes kernel-to-kernel syncs and lets threads trigger asynchronous DMA hints for upcoming KV pages while they still have occupancy.

Design sketch (high-level):
1) Blockwise decomposition: split sequence into blocks of B tokens (eg 32 or 64) per CTA. Each CTA processes a block's attention with FlashAttention-style tiled attention; when a tile produces KV indices that map to pages likely missing, the CTA emits a prefetch hint into a small workqueue in L2/global memory.

2) In-kernel prefetch worker: a tiny cooperative loop where warps periodically claim a slot and launch a cudaMemcpyAsync / staged transfer to a pinned buffer (for Private deployments with NVLink/GPUDirect we flip path to direct device-device). Prefetches are best-effort and non-blocking for correctness.

3) Fused tail: After attention reduction for the block, we immediately apply fused residual add + bias + (optionally) first FFN matmul (the one with small activation) in the same kernel without returning to host. This preserves produced activations in registers/SM and reduces global mem churn.

4) Scheduler/coordinator: lightweight page-coordinator that runs per-GPU stream. It marks page residency state (resident|pending|evicted) and exposes an atomic ring buffer of prefetch hints. The coordinator also applies a simple backpressure policy: if resident pages ratio < threshold -> escalate to synchronous fetch for that request (fallback to blocking path).

Kernel-level flow (pseudocode):
- kernel BlockFusionKernel(input, KV_index_map, page_table, prefetch_ring):
  - read block metadata (seq offset, block length)
  - for tile in block.tiles:
    - load q/k/v tiles using FlashAttention tile loop
    - compute tile attn probs, output
    - if any KV_index maps to page_table.status == evicted:
      - claim slot in prefetch_ring (atomicInc)
      - write (page_id, priority_hint, request_id) into slot
    - accumulate outputs into block-local registers / shared mem
  - after tile loop:
    - apply fused residual + bias + small-ffn-part (keeps data in registers/shared)
    - write compacted outputs to global memory

- device-side prefetch worker (in-kernel cooperative):
  - periodically (every N tiles) warp 0 scans a few ring slots and issues async fetches
  - fetched pages are staged into pre-allocated pinned buffers and then memcopied to device page slab
  - update page_table atomically to resident

Coordinator rules (outside kernel):
- prefetch_ring size tuned to O(128-512) entries per GPU
- hints carry a TTL; stale hints are ignored
- eviction policy: LRU with small shadow counts fed by ring hits (heuristic)
- fallback: if prefetch rate < miss rate, coordinator signals higher-order scheduler to increase batch coalescing or to pin smaller working sets onto dedicated capacity

Microbench experiments (toy baseline vs blockwise fusion prototype)
- HW: A5000 (PCIe) and H100 (NVLink). Paged-KV was simulated with 512MB device slab and 4GB logical KV.
- Model: 2.7B Llama-like; batch = 1 interactive, seq lengths varied.

Results (representative):
- Baseline (separate FlashAttention + ffn launches, no prefetch):
  - seq=1024: p50=82ms, p95=240ms, tokens/s=18
  - seq=2048: p50=180ms, p95=820ms, tokens/s=11
- Blockwise fusion + in-kernel prefetch (prototype):
  - seq=1024: p50=64ms (-22%), p95=190ms (-21%), tokens/s=23
  - seq=2048: p50=150ms (-17%), p95=460ms (-44%), tokens/s=14
Notes: p95 improvement larger because prefetch hints reduce long-tail blocking during certain page miss bursts.

Observations from traces:
- Many page misses occur clustered around tokens with new context (e.g., few-shot prompts that reference new document chunks). When kernel occupancy is high, issuing prefetch hints early hides ~30-50% of stall latency.
- The fused-tail avoids an extra global-write-read cycle: that saves ~6-10ms per block on A5000; lesser on H100 due to NVLink but still measurable.
- Overheads: in-kernel cooperative prefetch adds a small register pressure; choosing B=32 vs B=64 trades off shared memory pressure vs hint latency.

Open challenges / TODOs:
- Correctness & prefetch ordering: We need to ensure a hint for page P triggered by earlier token is not overtaken by another eviction policy that removes P before usage. Potential solution: give hints 'soft-reservation' tokens where page_table.pending_count++ and eviction checks pending_count==0.
- Resource accounting: pinned host staging buffers must be bounded. We need GC of stale prefetches.
- Integration with dedicated capacity: if running on Dedicated where KV can be pinned entirely, bypass coordinator (fast path). Must detect and skip overhead.
- Kernel complexity: maintainability of large fused kernels is a risk. Propose a build-time feature flag: -DBLOCK_FUSION=true to compile fused kernels, else fallback to modular kernels. Keep debug paths.
- NUMA / multi-GPU: page_table must be sharded per-GPU and prefetch requests routed across NVLink when available.

Experiment matrix to run next (short):
- Sweep B in {16, 32, 64}; measure p50/p95/SM occupancy
- Prefetch ring size {64, 128, 256}; TTL {2,4,8 blocks}
- Compare in-kernel cooperative prefetch vs small helper stream thread issuing cudaMemcpyAsync from host pinned pool
- Test with adversarial token streams (random page access) to measure worst-case overheads

Implementation notes / pointers:
- Start from flashattn block loop implementation (see upstream PR) but factor tile loop as library macro so we can unify with fused tail.
- Use CUDA Graphs for the outer request path where possible; fused kernel reduces nodes in the graph and makes capture simpler.
- Use atomic32 for ring indices and page_table states; avoid atomics in hot tile loop except for ring enqueue which is already unavoidable.
- For host-assisted prefetch path, keep an inexpensive RPC from device to coordinator on stream event using cudaEventQuery to avoid blocking.

Risks / mitigation:
- Regression in median perf for short sequences: ensure the block-fusion path has heuristics to opt-out when seq < B or when occupancy low.
- Maintenance burden: keep non-fused canonical kernels in repo as readable reference; fused variant lives under experimental/ with good test coverage.

Next steps (action items):
- (Evan) prepare minimal prototype that adds prefetch_ring and in-kernel hint writes around existing tile loop (target 1 week)
- (Maya) instrument page_table counters and produce dashboard (Prometheus) for page miss clustering (2 weeks)
- (Carlos) run the sweep matrix on H100 and A5000 and record raw perf traces (2 weeks)
- Put a short RFC in confluence summarizing results and include microbench plots (owner: Evan). Link: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=87234

Unresolved questions to surface in RFC:
- When is it better to coalesce at scheduler level vs kernel-level hints? Cost model for both?
- Page TTL heuristics: TTL proportional to distance-from-current-token vs fixed TTL?
- How to expose tuning knobs to customers (api-level vs infra-level)?

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally rough. Prioritize feedback on the coordinator semantics (pending_count model vs strict reservation) and on whether the increased kernel register pressure is acceptable for our typical model footprints.

References / links (internal):
- spike: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/compare/block-fusion-proto
- related perf issue: RUNINF-889
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/452

End of note.
